bullets: Reliability: repeat and get similar results?
Accuracy: close to the true value?
Validity: did we measure what we asked?

points: Conclusion: reliable for this site, less so in general

keywords.def: the answer to the enquiry question, backed by evidence
whether repeating the method would give similar results
how close results are to the true value
whether the method actually measured what the question asked
judging the strengths and limits of the enquiry

questions.q: What is the difference between reliability and accuracy?
questions.a: Reliability: repeatable results; accuracy: close to the true value

questions.q: Suggest one way to improve reliability.
questions.a: More trials, more sites, repeat on different days

questions.q: Why might soil moisture affect validity?
questions.a: Wet soil infiltrates slowly whatever the surface, so differences may not be due to surface type

questions.q: Core: In the portal response box write your conclusion (answer the question, accept or reject hypotheses with data) and evaluation (reliability, accuracy, validity, improvements).
questions.a: A data-backed conclusion and an evaluation using all three terms with realistic improvements

questions.q: Extend: (8 marks, own exam-style) Evaluate the reliability of your conclusions.
questions.a: Strengths and limits of methods and data, effect on confidence, a final judgement

questions.q: Stretch: How would you extend the enquiry to a whole drainage basin?
questions.a: Sample sites across land uses using GIS, plus river gauge data at several points

questions.q: If a method did not measure what the question asked, it lacks:
questions.a: B) Validity. Validity is about measuring the right thing to answer the question.
Did we measure the right thing?
